content.text: {"relation": "DIVERGENT", "consensus_summary": "All three blind responses converge on a primary meaning of faith as trusting reliance on and confident assurance in God/Christ — the divinely enabled instrument by which one is justified and saved (Hebrews 11:1; Ephesians 2:8-9; Romans 1:17; Galatians 2:16) — explicitly distinguished from mere intellectual assent. Faithfulness/covenant loyalty (the emunah/pistis-Christou reading) appears in every response, but only as a common secondary alternative, never as the primary definition.", "book_summary": "The book defines faith primarily as faithfulness: obedience held steady by hope in the promise, anchored in Habakkuk 2:4 (emunah as fidelity) and James 2:17 (faith without works is dead). Its common-view note explicitly flags — and sets itself against — the standard teaching that faith is confident trust functioning as the sole instrument of justification.", "rationale": "The book takes what the blind consensus uniformly treats as a secondary alternative (faithfulness/loyal obedience) and promotes it to the primary and apparently exclusive meaning, while its common-view note signals deliberate displacement of the mainstream 'trust as sole instrument of justification' definition. Because the book's meaning is recognizable within the consensus landscape (it is not NOVEL), but it contradicts and displaces the dominant reading rather than sharpening it, DIVERGENT is the correct classification rather than REFINED. A REFINED verdict would require the book to remain compatible with trust-as-primary; instead the entry recenters faith on obedience-plus-works, which cuts against the sola-fide framing all three responses identify as the settled core.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "The book's definition is not alien to the tradition: faithfulness/allegiance is listed as a 'common' alternative in all three blind responses (emunah in Habakkuk 2:4, pistis-Christou scholarship, James 2), and James 2:17 directly states the book's tagline. One could therefore argue the book merely elevates a well-attested strand of the semantic range — a REFINED narrowing rather than a true contradiction — especially since mainstream teaching also insists living faith produces obedience. However, the entry's own note frames the trust/justification view as the displaced 'common teaching,' which tips it into divergence.", "confidence": "high"}
